findings.title: Mythic+ keystone context never cleared; every later GameObject loot recorded as MPLUS
findings.evidence: State.keystone is set on CHALLENGE_MODE_START and deliberately kept after completion. It is cleared only in Attribution:Disable (:411); grep finds writes only at :229/:238/:411. ResolveLootSource maps any GameObject loot to S.MPLUS while state.keystone is set, so herbs, ore, world chests and other instances' containers are persisted to LootHistoryDB as MPLUS with a keystoneLevel. That pollutes the Source column and filter, the Insights by-source and keystone breakdowns (core/Database.lua:557-558) and both CSVs, with no repair. No test covers the context lifetime; only the pure resolver case at tests/test_attribution.lua:71 exists. Related, unverified: at :238 a completion-time 0 from GetActiveKeystoneLevel is truthy, so 0 would be stored.
findings.remediation: C-001: add a presence-guarded NS.Compat.InPartyInstance() shim (IsInInstance, instanceType == 'party'). Add Attribution:OnZoneChanged, which clears State.keystone when not in a party instance, and OnChallengeModeReset. Register ZONE_CHANGED_NEW_AREA and CHALLENGE_MODE_RESET on bus and append them to self.__events so Disable tears them down. Do NOT register PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD on NS.addon, which would collide with LifecycleSetup:112 OnEnterWorld. Guard :238 with (lvl and lvl > 0). Add 3 tests (clears when out of instance, kept in instance, CHALLENGE_MODE_RESET) and update the Enable 'seven events' case to nine. Update docs/data-flow.md:88 and midnight-quirks.md:22, and move test-cases.md and the badge in the same commit. Smoke S-001. Existing mislabelled rows cannot be repaired (no signal).
findings.verify_reason: modules/Attribution.lua:174-176 maps any GameObject to MPLUS while state.keystone is set. The only writes to keystone are :229 (start), :238 (completion keeps it) and :411 (Disable). Nothing clears it on leaving the instance, and a grep of core/modules/settings finds no ZONE_CHANGED or CHALLENGE_MODE_RESET handler. So every herb, ore or chest looted later in the session is persisted as MPLUS, and that shows up in the Source column and filter and in Database.lua:557. :238 uses `or`, so a completion-time 0 would be stored. Enable registers 7 events (:346-359) and tests/test_attribution.lua:396 pins 'seven'. The remediation is sound: it keeps PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD off NS.addon, where LifecycleSetup.lua:112 already binds OnEnterWorld.

findings.title: 25 vendored LibKa0s tags have no re-vendor bundle or register row
findings.evidence: Since the 2026-08-25 horizon, commits touching libs/LibKa0s vendored 31 distinct tags (read off CLAUDE.md provenance at each commit). docs/revendor/ records 8. The 25 unrecorded tags are v1.18.0, v1.18.1, v1.19.0, v1.23.0, v1.24.0, v1.26.0-v1.29.0, v1.35.0-v1.39.0 (incl. v1.36.1/.2), v1.42.0, v1.44.0, v1.45.0, v1.46.1, v1.47.0 and v1.50.0-v1.53.0. No bundle names a span and there is no Documented deviations row. The High grade is fixed by AUDIT.md step 4; by impact alone it would be Low, since no user reaches it.
findings.remediation: Write one consolidated bundle, docs/revendor/<date>-v1.53.0/. Its 01_DELTA.md line 1 names the span v1.15.0 -> v1.53.0, with a table of the 25 unrecorded tags and the vendoring commit of each (git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -- libs/LibKa0s). Its 05_SUMMARY.md states the intermediate tags were carried by sweeps with nothing adopted beyond the commits. Do not back-fill per-tag folders. Re-run the ledger commands and expect count=0. The later re-vendor (the LH-69 fix) must write its own bundle so this does not recur.
findings.rule_ref: audit-review-history (A re-vendor commit implies a bundle); AUDIT.md step 4
findings.verify_reason: I recomputed the provenance tags from CLAUDE.md for every libs/LibKa0s commit since 2026-08-25. There are 31 distinct tags. Recorded bundle delta lines cover v1.25, v1.31-v1.34 and v1.55, which leaves exactly the 25 listed unrecorded. audit-review-history.md:34 is a MUST, and :57 allows a single consolidated bundle naming the span. There is no Documented deviations row. High follows AUDIT.md, as the finding says. Side note: the new docs/revendor/2026-09-23-v1.55.0/01_DELTA.md line 1 says 'v1.54.2 -> v1.55.0', but this repo's previous vendored tag was v1.53.0 (v1.54.x never landed here). The consolidated bundle's span should end at v1.53.0, and that delta line's base should be noted or corrected in a new bundle rather than by editing the frozen one. The v1.55.0 re-vendor already has its own bundle, so the 'later re-vendor must write its own bundle' clause is already met.

findings.title: General visibility decides from InCombatLockdown(), so 'Only out of combat' fails to hide at the pull
findings.evidence: B:VisibilityAllows reads InCombatLockdown() for a purely visual decision, and B:ApplyVisibility runs from the PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED handler, where lockdown is not yet engaged (options-ui-§15 relies on that timing). BrowserTable's testModeRefusal reads the same flag. tests/test_browser.lua:627-636 set the mock's lockdown flag directly, so the suite cannot see the event timing. Not reproduced in the client.
findings.remediation: Make VisibilityAllows(inCombat) and ApplyVisibility(inCombat) take the edge explicitly: true from PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED, false from PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED, else UnitAffectingCombat('player'). Use UnitAffectingCombat for testModeRefusal too. Add UnitAffectingCombat to .luacheckrc read_globals. Add tests that fire PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED with mock lockdown false and assert the window hides under Only out of combat (red under an InCombatLockdown read), plus the mirror for Only in combat. Add a Version History note for the behavior change. Smoke S1: pull a dummy with Only out of combat set.
findings.verify_reason: Browser.lua:1135 decides visibility from InCombatLockdown(). ApplyVisibility is run by the PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED handler (:1246-1247), where lockdown is known not to be engaged yet. Nothing re-evaluates visibility later, so under 'Only out of combat' the window stays up for the whole fight. events-frames-taint.md §2 says UnitAffectingCombat SHOULD be used for display logic and PLAYER_REGEN_* for transitions, which is what the finding cites. BrowserTable.lua:543 has the same read. The remediation, passing the edge explicitly, is correct. It is in_game_only for confirmation.

findings.title: Encounter detail cleared at ENCOUNTER_END, before the boss corpse is looted
findings.evidence: OnEncounterEnd sets State.encounter = nil. The corpse's LOOT_OPENED comes after ENCOUNTER_END, so sourceDetail.encounterID and difficulty are effectively never written for boss loot. docs/data-flow.md:74 and docs/midnight-quirks.md:17 claim the field is captured. No UI displays the field, which caps severity. The event order needs in-client confirmation.
findings.remediation: C-002: on a successful ENCOUNTER_END (success == 1), keep State.encounter and stamp expires = GetTime() + Constants.ENCOUNTER_GRACE (a new constant, about 60 s). Clear it on a wipe. ResolveLootSource treats the encounter as live while now <= expires, with now passed via state in tests. Add 2 tests (within grace carries encounterID, after grace does not) and move the badge and inventory. Checkpoint CP-1 / smoke S-002 first: if LOOT_OPENED precedes ENCOUNTER_END in-client, close as not reproduced and make no code change (or document the field as not captured).
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. OnEncounterEnd (Attribution.lua:223-226) nils State.encounter, and in the client ENCOUNTER_END fires at the boss kill, before the corpse can be looted. So ResolveLootSource at :168-171 almost never attaches encounterID or difficulty, even though docs/data-flow.md:85 and midnight-quirks.md claim it does. Severity lowered to low: sourceDetail.encounterID is not displayed, filtered, exported to a visible column or aggregated anywhere (Collector.lua:68 says 'not displayed'). This is invisible metadata loss plus doc drift. The remediation is fine. Note that the grace window will also tag trash KILL loot within about 60 s after the boss; that is acceptable.

findings.title: Currency-category cache is built once per session and never rebuilt
findings.evidence: The id-to-header map is a snapshot taken at the session's first currency loot. A currency first discovered later, or one under a header that was collapsed at build time (unverified), is missing from it. Its row is persisted with itemSubType = nil and never backfilled. This hits routinely at season start.
findings.remediation: In Compat.CurrencyCategory, rebuild the cache at most once per miss (a module-local sentinel keyed by the missed id, so an id that is genuinely absent does not trigger a walk on every loot) and look it up again. Keep the unknown-id -> nil contract (test_compat.lua:338). For collapsed headers, either (a) verify in the client whether GetCurrencyListInfo exposes collapsed children and, if not, document the gap in midnight-quirks.md, or (b) expand collapsed headers for the walk via C_CurrencyInfo.ExpandCurrencyList, guarded for presence, and restore them afterwards. Add a test_compat case where the mock list gains an id after the first call. Smoke S-003.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. core/Compat.lua:390-393 builds currencyCategoryCache once and never invalidates it. A currency discovered after the first build misses, and Collector.lua:198 persists itemSubType=nil permanently, so the row falls out of the subtype filter (Database.lua:348). The remediation is incomplete for the collapsed-header case the finding itself raises. GetCurrencyListSize/GetCurrencyListInfo only enumerate children of expanded headers, so rebuild-on-miss cannot recover an id under a collapsed header. Also, tests/test_compat.lua:338 asserts that an unknown id returns nil, so a rebuild must not change that answer.

findings.title: Shortening 'Keep history for' deletes history immediately with no confirm
findings.evidence: The settings.retentionDays onChange calls NS.Database:PruneOld() directly. A mis-click in the dropdown, or /lh set settings.retentionDays 7, irreversibly drops older records in the same action. /lh purge, by contrast, goes through the KA0S_LOOTHISTORY_PURGE confirm. No test pins this onChange today.
findings.remediation: Keep the Schema:Set write (architecture-§5). Add Database:CountOlderThan(days) and do nothing when it is 0. Otherwise show a KA0S_LOOTHISTORY_PRUNE StaticPopup naming N, following the house pair: Yes/No, timeout=0, whileDead, hideOnEscape. Accept runs PruneOld. Decline should restore the previous retention value through Schema:Set, so that declining actually protects the records, and print one line saying so. Headless, or with no StaticPopup_Show, keep the immediate prune. Add tests in tests/test_schema.lua for popup present (no prune before accept, and decline restores) and popup absent (prunes). Update docs/settings-panel.md. Drop the options-ui-§12 rule_ref; there is no standards rule behind this.
findings.verify_reason: The behaviour is real. settings/Schema.lua:370-375 onChange calls NS.Database:PruneOld() immediately, so a dropdown mis-click or '/lh set settings.retentionDays 7' deletes older records with no confirm, while /lh purge is confirmed (Slash.lua:8-18). The rule_ref is wrong: options-ui.md §12 governs only the global reset act and its wording, not retention changes, so this is a UX/data-safety finding with no standards backing. The remediation's decline path only defers the deletion to the next login rather than preventing it, which is weak protection.

findings.title: Degraded Slash stub refusal line drifted from lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT
findings.evidence: The stub renders '... enable it with /lh' while claiming to be byte-identical to the library, which renders '<brand> ... /lh enable'. That breaks the canonical refusal-line shape. On that path, enable itself is unavailable, so the line points at nothing that works. Reachable only on a library-less install with settings.enabled=false.
findings.remediation: C-005: format the stub line with '/lh enable' (slash .. ' enable'), and correct the comment to note that enable is unavailable on the library-less path. Better still, drop the stub's own format string. Add a +1 parity case in the degraded block of tests/test_slash.lua comparing the stub output to lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT:format(NS.BRAND, '/lh enable') with the library loaded. Smoke S-005. Re-check after any LibKa0s re-vendor in case the library format moved.
findings.verify_reason: The drift is real. settings/Slash.lua:255-257 formats the line with '/lh', while the library (libs/LibKa0s/Slash.lua:596) passes slash..' enable'. The format string itself is identical to lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT (:83), so the 'byte-identical' comment is wrong about the argument, not the template. Severity lowered to low. It is reachable only on a library-less install, which cannot happen with the vendored payload, and it also needs settings.enabled=false. On that path, enable is in UNAVAILABLE_WITHOUT_LIB (:282-286), so neither '/lh' nor '/lh enable' leads anywhere that works. The fix is a parity and comment correction only.

findings.title: AH priority list re-parsed per record on every Stats/export pass; accumulateTime calls date() twice per record
findings.evidence: AuctionPrice:Pick calls cfg() and runs tag:match('^(.-):(.+)$') on each priority tag, up to 11 allocating matches per record. It is reached once per record in Database:Stats and 3-4 times per CSV row. accumulateTime calls date() twice per record, and date('*t') allocates a table. Both violate the loop-invariant hoist rule stated at core/Database.lua:307-313. Unverified: there is no perf runner or capture.
findings.remediation: Measure first with an uncommitted micro-benchmark over a large synthetic history, and act only if it shows a real cost. If it does, memoize tag parsing in a module-local table keyed by the tag string (tag -> prov, key). Tag strings are immutable, so this needs no invalidation, no bus target and no stand-down change. In Stats/Export, read cfg() once per call and pass the priority list to Pick (for example Pick(map, priority)). For accumulateTime, cache the day string per ts//86400 within one Stats call. Add a test that Pick honours a reorder after MovePriorityWithin. Drop the events-frames-taint-§7 rule_ref.
findings.verify_reason: The code shape is real. AuctionPrice:Pick (modules/AuctionPrice.lua:91-100) calls cfg() and tag:match per priority tag for each record. It is reached per record from Util.RecordValue in Database:Stats and 3 times per CSV row (Export.lua:96-100). accumulateTime (Database.lua:534-539) calls date() twice. The rule_ref is misapplied: events-frames-taint.md §7 governs per-frame loops (OnUpdate/OnEvent), and Stats and Export are user-initiated, not per-frame. The Database.lua:307-313 comment scopes its hoist rule to QueryList. Nothing was measured, so severity is low. The proposed fix (a compiled plan, a new SETTINGS_CHANGED bus target, and an addition to the stand-down list) adds a registration and invalidation surface out of proportion to an unmeasured cost.

findings.title: tests/test_debuglog.lua unit-tests the library's own formatter
findings.evidence: Four cases (FormatPlain wraps/renders the tag, tolerates a nil tag, FormatColored colors) test LibKa0s-DebugLog rendering, not addon wiring. A legitimate upstream formatter change would turn them red while the library suite is green.
findings.remediation: C-007: delete the four cases and keep the FONT_MONO and NS.Debug / NS.SafeToString integration cases. That is -4 cases; move docs/test-cases.md and the README badge in the same commit. The cases belong in LibKa0s's suite, which already owns that behavior.
findings.verify_reason: Real. tests/test_debuglog.lua:10-28 holds four cases that pin LibKa0s-DebugLog's FormatPlain/FormatColored output. The exact color strings appear at libs/LibKa0s/DebugLog.lua:123. testing-§8 (WowAddonStandards standards/testing.md:139-145) says the addon MUST NOT keep a duplicate copy of library cases, so the rule citation is accurate. I lowered severity to low because the only reachable impact is a red addon suite after a legitimate upstream formatter change. There is no runtime or user impact. The remediation is right: keep the FONT_MONO case (:4-8) and the NS.Debug/SafeToString secret-sink cases, and update docs/test-cases.md and the README badge in the same commit. Deleting these four cases does not affect the _frameForTest/_toggleClickForTest seams that test_surface_parity.lua:142-146 says test_debuglog drives, because those come from other cases in the file.

findings.title: DebugLog degradation stub copies library formatters and colors with no caller
findings.evidence: The stub's FormatPlain/FormatColored repeat the library's format strings and color codes (|cff6f8faf, |cffc9a66b). A grep finds no addon non-test caller; only tests/test_debuglog.lua reaches these members, and it reaches the live library instance. The copy is inert and will go stale.
findings.remediation: Keep both members on the stub, but make each one return tostring(msg), or a plain concatenation with no color codes, so no library format string lives in the addon and the surface-parity case stays green without an ignore-list change. The alternative is to remove them and add "FormatPlain" and "FormatColored" to the ignore list at tests/test_surface_parity.lua:129, with the zero-caller grep in the comment. Land this together with R-07.
findings.verify_reason: Real. The stub at core/DebugLogSetup.lua:34-40 repeats the library's plain format and its colored format string byte for byte (|cff6f8faf...|cffc9a66b, libs/LibKa0s/DebugLog.lua:123). No non-test code under core/, modules/ or settings/ calls FormatPlain or FormatColored. The only callers are in tests/test_debuglog.lua, and they reach the live instance. #47 exempts degradation stubs only in the shapes it names, and a copied formatter is not one of them. I lowered severity to low because the copy is inert: no caller reaches it on the degraded path, so there is no user impact, only drift risk. On the remediation: tests/test_surface_parity.lua:123-150 asserts the stub carries the whole live surface minus an ignore list. Returning tostring(msg) keeps parity with no test change. Dropping the members requires adding FormatPlain and FormatColored to that ignore list together with the grep that shows zero callers, as the existing entries do.

findings.title: Event-registration blocks are not isolated per event and nothing records rejected event names
findings.locations: modules/Attribution.lua:349-355, modules/Attribution.lua:369, modules/Collector.lua:218-219, modules/Browser.lua:1246, modules/Browser.lua:1252, core/LifecycleSetup.lua:112
findings.evidence: Every registration is a bare call. A retired event name would raise, and every registration after it in the block would go unbound silently. A grep for IsEventValid, __badEvents or rejected in core, modules and settings finds nothing. This is latent: every name is valid on 12.1. The C_EventUtils.IsEventValid SHOULD is also unmet.
findings.remediation: Add NS.SafeRegister(target, event, handler, unit), which front-gates with C_EventUtils.IsEventValid and pcalls the register, plus NS.RejectedEvents, in core/LifecycleSetup.lua or core/Util.lua. Route every block through it. Keep Attribution.__events as the names that actually registered, so Disable stays symmetric. Surface the list via /lh debug events and a clause in the [Init] summary. Add C_EventUtils to .luacheckrc. Test with the kit's M.__badEvents (ENCOUNTER_START): the other six still register and the rejected list names it. tests/test_disabled.lua must still reach an empty set. Smoke S2.
findings.verify_reason: The cited code matches. Attribution.lua:349-355 has seven bare bus:RegisterEvent calls and :369 has a bare RegisterUnitEvent. Collector.lua:218-219, Browser.lua:1246/1252 and LifecycleSetup.lua:112 are also bare. A grep of core/, modules/ and settings/ finds no IsEventValid, rejected-list or pcall guard. The rule is events-frames-taint-§1 ('An unknown event name raises...', standards/events-frames-taint.md). It requires a MUST for per-event pcall isolation and a MUST that rejected names are recorded and reachable from the debug verb or console. The IsEventValid front-gate is a SHOULD, so the finding reads the rule correctly. All current names are valid, so the defect is latent and low is right. No LibKa0s module provides a safe-register helper; I grepped libs/LibKa0s. An addon-local helper is therefore correct, and it is not the forbidden frame factory because it creates no frames. The kit mock supports M.__badEvents (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:715-725), so the proposed test works. Also note the event-to-edge trade in the quirks doc, as §1 says.

findings.title: core\CoreSetup.lua load-bearing TOC position is unannotated
findings.evidence: core/CoreSetup.lua:180 builds the printer at file scope with lib:New({ prefix = NS.PREFIX }), where NS.PREFIX is published by core/Namespace.lua:18. TOC line 48 is bare.
findings.remediation: Add a comment above LootHistory.toc:48 naming both constraints: 'LOAD-BEARING: lib:New{ prefix = NS.PREFIX } runs at file load (core\Namespace.lua must be above), and NS.Print, published here, is captured as a file-scope local by modules\Browser.lua, settings\Schema.lua and settings\Slash.lua (must be below them).' Put it in one TOC commit with A-05, A-06 and A-07, and keep the tests/test_harness.lua TOC-derivation cases green.
findings.verify_reason: Real. The TOC entry at LootHistory.toc:48 has no comment. core/CoreSetup.lua:180 runs lib:New({ prefix = NS.PREFIX }) at file scope, and NS.PREFIX comes from core/Namespace.lua:18 (TOC :45). The position is also load-bearing the other way, which the finding missed. modules/Browser.lua:5, settings/Schema.lua:5 and settings/Slash.lua:4 all capture NS.Print into a local when they load, so CoreSetup must stay above them. toc-file-§5 requires a MUST comment naming what resolves at load, one row per position, so the citation and severity are fine. The remediation's comment names only half of the constraint.

findings.title: core\DebugLogSetup.lua load-bearing TOC position is unannotated
findings.evidence: The file-load lib:New{...} descriptor at core/DebugLogSetup.lua:76-90 reads NS.Constants.FONT_MONO, which is resolved at core/Constants.lua:64. TOC line 56 is bare.
findings.remediation: Add a comment above LootHistory.toc:56: LOAD-BEARING: the descriptor reads NS.Constants.FONT_MONO at :New; core\Constants.lua must be above. Same commit as LH-56.
findings.verify_reason: The TOC entry at LootHistory.toc:56 (core\DebugLogSetup.lua) has no comment. The file-scope lib:New descriptor passes font = NS.Constants.FONT_MONO (core/DebugLogSetup.lua around :90). That value is resolved at core/Constants.lua:64, which is TOC :44. Moving the line up would be a silent, load-time font failure, which is the load-bearing case in toc-file-§5. One MUST row at low severity is right.

findings.title: settings\Slash.lua load-bearing TOC position is unannotated
findings.evidence: The dispatcher is built at file scope with commands = NS.COMMANDS (assigned at Schema.lua:739) and brandName = NS.BRAND. Moved above Schema, it would get nil and every verb would silently go unknown. TOC line 87 is bare.
findings.remediation: Add a comment above LootHistory.toc:87: 'LOAD-BEARING: the dispatcher is built at file load with commands = NS.COMMANDS, assigned by settings\Schema.lua; below Schema, LibKa0s-Slash :New raises and /lh is never registered.' Land it in the same TOC commit as A-04.
findings.verify_reason: Real. The TOC entry at LootHistory.toc:87 has no comment. settings/Slash.lua:355-358 calls lib:New with commands = NS.COMMANDS at file scope, and NS.COMMANDS is assigned at settings/Schema.lua:739. The finding gets the failure mode wrong, though. The vendored libs/LibKa0s/Slash.lua:480 does error(MAJOR .. ':New requires descriptor.commands', 2), so a Slash.lua moved above Schema would raise at load and never build the dispatcher. It would not quietly leave every verb unknown. brandName = NS.BRAND is from core/Namespace.lua:13, so it is not a Schema dependency. The annotation is still required under the toc-file-§5 MUST and low stands. Only the evidence and the comment text change.

findings.title: Conventional TOC groups don't say they are conventional; PoolSetup comment claims a position (dependent of LH-56)
findings.evidence: # Locales (:29), # Defaults (:67) and the plain # Core run (Constants, Namespace, State, Util, LootHistory, Database) carry no 'free to move' statement. The PoolSetup comment at :57 states a position, but nothing resolves at load: every NS.Pool call is inside a function. SHOULD, derived from LH-56.
findings.remediation: In the LH-56 commit, add a one-line conventional note per group and reword the PoolSetup comment as conventional.
findings.verify_reason: # Locales (:29), # Defaults (:67) and the Core run at :44-47 and :59-60 have no conventional-or-free note. The PoolSetup comment at :57 ('Before every module that pools a widget') claims an ordering. Every NS.Pool.New call is inside functions (for example modules/Analytics.lua:616-637, inside the build function), and no file captures NS.Pool at file scope, so the position is conventional. toc-file-§5 grades this as one SHOULD row per file, never per line. Low is correct, and landing it in the same commit as A-04 is fine.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md hub is 554 lines; Settings schema section past the ~60-line spill threshold
findings.evidence: The hub is 554 lines against a ~400-line SHOULD (458 at the last run; issue #31 was closed done at 490). ## Settings schema is 68 lines against the ~60-line MUST and carries five links. ## The disabled state is 79 lines but is not a mandated section. Carried and grown.
findings.remediation: Spill the named-state and registry paragraphs of Settings schema (:118-160) into schema.md and leave a summary of 15 lines or fewer with one link. Move The disabled state body to a Tier 3 docs/disabled-state.md registered in ### Addon-specific. Re-measure: hub under 400 lines, section at 60 or fewer.
findings.verify_reason: `wc -l docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` = 554. ## Settings schema runs from :95 to :163, which is about 69 lines, against the ~60-line spill MUST, and it carries several links rather than one. ## The disabled state (:255-334) is about 79 lines. The standard says the numbers are approximate, but 554 against 400 and 69 against 60 are both real overruns. Low is right.

findings.title: Nine bus-message string literals at Send/RegisterMessage call sites in tests
findings.locations: tests/test_browser.lua:536, tests/test_browser.lua:552, tests/test_collector.lua:440, tests/test_collector.lua:444, tests/test_collector.lua:473, tests/test_harness.lua:145, tests/test_harness.lua:146, tests/test_panel.lua:232, tests/test_panel.lua:252
findings.evidence: The grep (Send|Register)Message("Ka0s_ outside libs/ and tests/_kit/ finds 9 hits, all in tests. A typo'd literal would send to nobody and the case would pass vacuously. Production code has none.
findings.remediation: Use NS.MSG.RECORD_ADDED, HISTORY_CHANGED and SETTINGS_CHANGED. In tests/test_harness.lua, declare local PROBE = 'Ka0s_LootHistory_HarnessProbe' once. The literal assertions in tests/test_constants.lua stay. Re-run the grep and expect 0.
findings.verify_reason: The grep over *.lua outside libs/ and tests/_kit/ still returns exactly the 9 cited hits (test_browser.lua:536,552; test_collector.lua:440,444,473; test_harness.lua:145,146; test_panel.lua:232,252). architecture-§4 (WowAddonStandards architecture.md, the closed-bus bullet) says the constant MUST be used 'at every SendMessage and RegisterMessage call site — never the literal' and that each Ka0s_ literal should appear once in the repo. Test files are call sites too. NS.MSG is a strict Bus.Catalog (core/Constants.lua:191-209) with RECORD_ADDED, HISTORY_CHANGED and SETTINGS_CHANGED, so the remediation works. The harness probe is test-only, so a single local constant is the right fix. There is no production impact, so low is correct.

findings.title: Unresolvable standard citations: disabled-§7 test names and packaging.md:28 in .pkgmeta
findings.evidence: 12 test names cite disabled-§7 or disabled-§7.N, but there is no disabled section file, and 11 of them use the retired dotted form. docs/test-cases.md mirrors them. .pkgmeta cites packaging.md:28, a line number into a file with no numbered subsections whose line 28 no longer carries the rule.
findings.remediation: Rename the cases to 'slash-commands-§7 step N: ...' and regenerate docs/test-cases.md (the count stays 858). Cite 'packaging' (bare filename) in .pkgmeta. Re-run the sweep: 0 disabled-§ hits, 0 dotted §N.M hits.
findings.verify_reason: tests/test_disabled.lua:174-516 has 12 test names citing 'disabled-§7' or 'disabled-§7.N'. No disabled.md section file exists. The rule is slash-commands.md '### 7. The disabled state is total', and its conformance suite has numbered steps 1-10, so 'slash-commands-§7 step N' resolves. docs/test-cases.md has 12 hits. .pkgmeta:14,19,20 cite 'packaging.md:28'. Line 28 of packaging.md is '- _dev', packaging.md has no numbered subsections, and a line citation does not parse as filename-§N. documentation-§6 grades malformed references as a MUST fix and the dotted form as a SHOULD. The finding is accurate.

findings.title: No surface-parity case for the Env, Item, Media, Pool and Lifecycle stubs
findings.locations: tests/test_surface_parity.lua:66-214, core/EnvSetup.lua, core/ItemSetup.lua:40-67, core/MediaSetup.lua, core/PoolSetup.lua:24-52, core/LifecycleSetup.lua:148-162
findings.evidence: Parity cases exist for Core, Widgets, Slash, DebugLog, Options, Bus, Compat and Schema. Five adopted modules with library-absent branches have none. Every member reached today is answered, so this is a gate gap, not a live crash. Launcher has no stub by written decision.
findings.remediation: Add five parity cases, by-name or two-table, each with a '-- members from: grep ...' comment and the degraded arm from tests/degraded_env.lua. Verify each goes red when a stub member is deleted and record that mutation (testing-§12). Move the badge and inventory in the same commit.
findings.verify_reason: tests/test_surface_parity.lua has cases only for Core, Widgets, Slash, DebugLog, Options, Bus, Compat and Schema (lines 66-213). testing-§8's stub-surface parity MUST requires a case 'per adopted LibKa0s module', with members found by grep, both arms checked, and the degraded arm built from a partial file list. Three modules have real library-absent stubs and no parity case: Item (NS.Item = Item or {...}, core/ItemSetup.lua), Pool (NS.Pool = Pool or {...}, core/PoolSetup.lua) and Lifecycle (hand-built NS.Lifecycle table with Hold, Release, Set, IsHeld, IsDown, Reevaluate, Holds and PrintHolds in core/LifecycleSetup.lua). Env and Media publish the same NS functions on both paths with internal branches, the same pattern as the Core seam case, so their cases will be mostly by-name checks. They are still required by the per-module wording. No live crash, so low.

findings.title: Vendored runner always records the perf skip as 'no tests/perf.lua', never the ratified performance-§12 exemption
findings.evidence: Every manifest has skipReason 'no tests/perf.lua — this addon ships no offline scenarios', and the RESULTS Perf prose says the skip is not the exemption. But the addon holds the ratified performance-§12 row (issue #22), and automated-tests-§3 says reason (2) MUST be recorded, naming performance-§12. The runner (kit revision 25) has no input that would let it know. testing-§1 forbids a local kit edit.
findings.remediation: Upstream first, in LibKa0s/testkit/run-automated-tests.sh. Before falling back to reason (1), detect a performance-§12 row in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ## Documented deviations, or accept an explicit env/flag override. Emit skipReason 'performance-§12 no-combat-path exemption (ratified; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md -> Documented deviations)' and branch the RESULTS Perf section on it. Add kit cases for with-row, without-row, and unparseable register (fails loudly). Release a tag, re-vendor the whole of LibKa0s (libs/LibKa0s + tests/_kit, provenance line and +x bit in the same commit) with its own docs/revendor bundle, then run the four suites so the new bundle records reason (2). Never hand-edit RESULTS.md or frozen bundles.
findings.verify_reason: tests/_kit/run-automated-tests.sh:343-344 sets NOTE[perf] to 'no tests/perf.lua — this addon ships no offline scenarios' whenever tests/perf.lua is absent. The md_perf_section at :838-841 says outright that the skip is not a performance-§12 exemption. All 11 manifests carry that skipReason. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:485 holds a ratified performance-§12 row. automated-tests-§3 sanctions exactly two perf skipReasons and says the exemption 'MUST be recorded when it applies, naming performance-§12'. LibKa0s testkit/run-automated-tests.sh (HEAD 46ccaa6) has only the same negative wording at :841. The fix therefore belongs upstream in LibKa0s, followed by a whole re-vendor, as the finding says.

findings.title: docs/performance.md is 190 lines; the exempt shape must be one screen
findings.evidence: Under the exemption the page must shrink to one screen: it brackets nothing, which of (b)/(c) applies, where the sweep lives, and what re-arms it. It currently carries the 77-line sweep, two allocation essays and a complexity section.
findings.remediation: Cut the page to one screen. Move the sweep to a Tier 3 docs/combat-path-sweep.md registered in the map, linked from the page and from the performance-§12 register row. Drop or relocate the allocation and complexity material. Keep tests/test_doc_structure.lua green.
findings.verify_reason: docs/performance.md is 190 lines. It has sections for Why, the 77-line sweep (:53-129), What ends the exemption, two allocation sections (:141, :157) and complexity (:185). documentation-§3 (documentation.md:193) says that under the exemption the page 'shrinks to one screen' stating that it brackets nothing, which of (b)/(c) applies, where the committed sweep lives, and what re-arms it. performance-§12 repeats this ('shrinks to a one-screen page ... and where the sweep lives'). Both texts assume the sweep lives somewhere other than this page. Moving it to a registered Tier 3 doc is compliant.

findings.title: README Usage does not close on a one-sentence configuration signpost
findings.evidence: The closing paragraph runs six sentences: configuration, then the enable/disable explanation, then the disabled slash surface. §1 requires one sentence and nothing more.
findings.remediation: Move the disabled-state sentences into the Usage body (or FAQ/Troubleshooting). End Usage on one sentence naming Settings ▸ AddOns and /lh help or /loothistory help. Run a de-AI pass.
findings.verify_reason: README.md:58, the last paragraph of ## Usage before ## How attribution works at :60, runs six sentences: the configuration pointer, then enable/disable, off-means-off, the live command surface and the feature-verb refusal. documentation-§1 (documentation.md, the Usage item) says 'Close with one line pointing at configuration, and nothing more ... both the short and long forms. One sentence. It is a signpost, not a summary.'

findings.title: Root CLAUDE.md sections out of mandated order (provenance before green gate)
findings.evidence: ## Vendored LibKa0s (with the provenance line at :51) precedes ## Green gate at :62. §2 orders the green-gate line (5) before the provenance line (6).
findings.remediation: Swap the two sections. The vendor gate greps rather than reading a position; keep tests/test_vendor_sync.lua green.
findings.verify_reason: CLAUDE.md headings are: H1 :1, Standards compliance :6, Read the docs :28, Vendored LibKa0s :49 (the provenance line is at :51), Green gate :62. documentation-§2 says the stub MUST contain its items 'in this order', with 5 the green-gate line and 6 the provenance line. The vendor_sync gate greps the pattern and does not check position, so swapping the sections is safe.

findings.title: Doc citations drifted from the tree (DEPENDENCIES.md, ARCHITECTURE.md)
findings.locations: DEPENDENCIES.md:49, DEPENDENCIES.md:53, DEPENDENCIES.md:112, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:42-45, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:207, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:447, docs/module-map.md
findings.evidence: DEPENDENCIES.md:53 cites run-automated-tests.sh :186/:109, now :242/:122 after the v1.55.0 re-vendor. :49 and :112 cite docs/testing.md:187/:179, now :191/:183. ARCHITECTURE.md:42-45 names four load-bearing seams (Item, Media, Widgets, Pool), but CoreSetup and DebugLogSetup are load-bearing too and Pool resolves nothing at load. :207 cites slash-commands-§4 for bare /lh, but the rule is §3. :447's compat trigger says '419 lines' where the trigger is a shim count (21).
findings.remediation: Re-point the citations: DEPENDENCIES.md:53 to run-automated-tests.sh:242 (declare -A) and :122 (EPOCHREALTIME); DEPENDENCIES.md:49 to docs/testing.md:191; DEPENDENCIES.md:112 to docs/testing.md:183. Change ARCHITECTURE.md:207 to cite slash-commands-§3. Write the :447 trigger as '21 shims (grep -cE '^\s*function\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\.' core/Compat.lua)'. Restate the load-bearing set in ARCHITECTURE.md:42-48 and docs/module-map.md from evidence in the tree: Item and Media above Constants; CoreSetup above every file that captures NS.Print at load (modules/Browser.lua:5, settings/Schema.lua:5, settings/Slash.lua:4); Widgets below Media; OptionsSetup above Schema. Call Pool conventional, since nothing resolves at load. Include DebugLogSetup only if a file-load capture of NS.Debug or NS.DebugLog is found. Keep the TOC comments in the same commit, consistent with that set.
findings.verify_reason: Most citations are confirmed. In DEPENDENCIES.md, 'declare -A ST DUR NOTE' is now at run-automated-tests.sh:242 (cited :186) and EPOCHREALTIME at :122 (cited :109). The luacheck 0/0 line is now docs/testing.md:191 (cited :187) and the regenerate line :183 (cited :179). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:207 cites slash-commands-§4 for bare /lh, but the bare-/<slash> MUST is at slash-commands.md:93, inside §3 (lines 41-98). ARCHITECTURE.md:447 uses a 419-line count. documentation-§3's trigger counts shims with grep -cE '^\s*function\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\.' core/Compat.lua, which returns 21 today. The load-bearing claim needed one fix. CoreSetup IS load-bearing: modules/Browser.lua:5, settings/Schema.lua:5 and settings/Slash.lua:4 capture NS.Print at file load. Pool does resolve nothing at load (NS.Pool.New is called only inside a function body, modules/Analytics.lua:616). But I found no file-load capture of NS.Debug or NS.DebugLog below DebugLogSetup; every use, e.g. core/Database.lua:12, is guarded and runs at runtime. The remediation should not assert DebugLog is load-bearing unless evidence shows it. It also should not depend on TOC comments from other findings (LH-56/57/63) that are not in the tree yet; the current TOC marks only Item, Media and Options load-bearing.

findings.title: Deconstruct attribution matches localized spell names with no localization-§4 register row
findings.evidence: Seed ids resolve to client-locale names (:64), and cast names are matched against them (:94). This is locale-correct by construction and reasoned in comments and closed issue #2. But the MUST says never by a localized display string, and a departure reasoned only in comments is not ratified.
findings.remediation: Add a localization-§4 row to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ## Documented deviations. Why: per-herb/ore Mass Mill/Prospect ids are not enumerable, and the names are derived from ids on the same client, so there is no English literal (cite :20-50 and #2). Trigger: Blizzard exposes a stable deconstruct token or category, or the id set becomes enumerable. Alternatively, replace the fallback with an id list.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Attribution.lua:20-50 (NAME_SEEDS), :64 seedToken resolves via NS.Compat.GetSpellName, :94 cast:find(tok) compares localized cast name. localization.md §4 (line 71+) MUST identify spells by spellID, 'never by a localized display string', and 'names never flow back into logic'. Locale-correct by construction (issue #2 CLOSED 'localize deconstruct name-matching'), but no localization-§4 row exists in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Documented deviations (grep empty); comment-only reasoning. Real, low.

findings.title: schemaVersion held at 1 in defaults while migrations stamp to 8, reasoned only in a comment
findings.evidence: versioning-git: MUST increment schemaVersion in defaults whenever an SV migration is required. The defaults hold 1, and the runner walks to 8. The comment gives a real reason (a seeded stamp would claim migrations that never ran under the AceDB backfill), and open-evolutions records this as the unruled 'Migration-stamp ownership' case. The rule conflicts with the runner shape savedvariables-§1 prints.
findings.remediation: Local: add a versioning-git register row citing the comment and open-evolutions 'Migration-stamp ownership', with trigger 'the standard rules on migration-stamp ownership'. Upstream (WowAddonStandards, not blocking): propose that versioning-git defer to the migration-stamp ruling, or state that the runner's highest 'to' is the version and the defaults value is the pre-migration floor. This resolves the conflict with savedvariables-§1.
findings.verify_reason: defaults/Global.lua:6-13 holds schemaVersion = 1 with the floor rationale in a comment; core/Database.lua MIGRATIONS ladder reaches to = 8 (:103) and RunMigrations (:127-138) stamps per step. versioning-git.md:8 MUST 'increment schemaVersion (in defaults) whenever a SV migration is required'; savedvariables.md:18-24 prints the runner shape starting from g.schemaVersion or 1; open-evolutions.md:15 carries 'Migration-stamp ownership' as open. No versioning-git row in ARCHITECTURE.md register. Local register row + non-blocking upstream proposal is correct routing.

findings.title: Resize grip draws Blizzard UI-ChatIM-SizeGrabber where the LibKa0s catalog ships 'resize'
findings.evidence: The grip uses the Blizzard SizeGrabber textures. The catalog carries 'resize'. The choice is argued only in a comment at :1042-1046 (matching the collection's corner grabbers), with no register row.
findings.remediation: Either draw NS.Icon('resize') (tinted like the other title-bar marks, with a hover tint) with the Blizzard grabber as the fallback rung, or add a library-stack-§8 register row. Optional upstream: since the argument is collection-wide, propose in WowAddonStandards (standalone-windows / library-stack-§8) whether the resize grip is a catalog mark or the Blizzard grabber, which would close it for every addon at once. Not blocking; either local path closes it. Smoke S3 if the mark is adopted. This touches the same line as LootHistory-R-09 (Lock frame gating), so coordinate the two.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Browser.lua:1042-1048 draws Interface\ChatFrame\UI-ChatIM-SizeGrabber-Up/Highlight with a comment-only argument; libs/LibKa0s/Media.lua:103 lists 'resize' and media/icons/resize.tga exists. library-stack.md §8 (line ~328) 'Where the addon needs a mark, it MUST use the catalog's'. No library-stack-§8 row in the register. Note the same Blizzard grabber is drawn in BankLedger/modules/Browser.lua, BankLedger/modules/SessionWindow.lua and MultiMeters/modules/Window.lua, so the optional upstream ruling is well-founded (collection-wide), but the local fix remains non-upstream (nothing under libs/ is edited).

findings.title: Analytics.lua watch-list 'Peel next' disposition has nothing tracking it
findings.evidence: modules/Analytics.lua has read 'Peel next' for seven runs since 20260804-233322, with no issue in gh issue list --state all. The file is now 1200 lines. The three-release clock has not started (only one release run), so this is not counted as a MUST failure. The review's Known follow-ups also names the Analytics peel as an open watch-list item.
findings.remediation: gh issue create 'Peel modules/Analytics.lua: renderers vs formatting/segmenting helpers' with labels state:triaged and severity:low (throttled), or do the peel. At the next automated-tests run, set the Disposition to 'already tracked as #N', the only hand edit RESULTS.md permits.
findings.rule_ref: automated-tests-§4 / performance-§10 (anti-pattern #53); MUST NOT not yet reached
findings.verify_reason: docs/automated-tests/RESULTS.md:84 row for modules/Analytics.lua reads 'Peel next ... Nothing tracks it' (file now 1200 lines by wc -l); gh issue list --state all --search Analytics shows only #7, #8, #27, none a peel issue. RESULTS itself says not yet past the three-release-run shelf life. Minor evidence nit: RESULTS says 'six runs running', the finding says seven (the count may include the latest run); immaterial.

findings.title: Window resize grip ignores Lock frame
findings.evidence: The grip's OnMouseDown calls StartSizing with no B:IsLocked() check, while the title-bar drag checks it. SaveWindow persists the resize. docs/settings-panel.md:40 defines Lock frame as drag-only, so this is an expectation gap, not a contract break.
findings.remediation: C-009: add 'if B:IsLocked() then return end' before frame:StartSizing('BOTTOMRIGHT'). Update docs/settings-panel.md:40 and :191 to say 'dragged or resized'. Smoke S-007. Coordinate with LH-76, which touches the same grip.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Browser.lua:1049 grip OnMouseDown calls frame:StartSizing('BOTTOMRIGHT') unconditionally; title-bar OnDragStart at :958-961 checks B:IsLocked(). OnMouseUp calls SaveWindow, so the resize persists. docs/settings-panel.md:40 says 'stop ... being dragged' and :191 describes gating only OnDragStart handlers, so this is an expectation gap as stated. Fix and doc update are correct.

All four accurate.

findings.title: Two stale line citations in docs/midnight-quirks.md

findings.title: Two vocabularies for bind state across exports and sentinels
findings.evidence: The row CSV uses 'Bind on Pickup' / 'Not Bound'. The Insights CSV uses 'Soulbound' / 'Unbound'. Database uses both the 'NONE' (:357) and 'UNBOUND' (:524) sentinels for the same state.
findings.remediation: C-011: unify both exports on the row-CSV labels (BOUND_LABEL_CSV reads from BOUND_LABEL, with UNBOUND mapped to NONE). Update tests/test_export.lua:217 from 'Unbound' to 'Not Bound' as an intended output change, and note it in the release notes. Leave the sentinels (NONE is a persisted savedView.bound key; UNBOUND keys Analytics/BrowserTable styling), but add comments at Database.lua:357 and :524 naming the other sentinel and why they differ. Smoke S-008.1.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Export.lua:11-14 BOUND_LABEL uses 'Not Bound'/'Bind on Pickup'; :140-141 BOUND_LABEL_CSV uses 'Soulbound'/'BoE'/'Warbound (UE)'/'Unbound'. core/Database.lua:357 uses r.bound or 'NONE', :524 uses r.bound or 'UNBOUND'. tests/test_export.lua:217 asserts 'A-Realm / Unbound'. Remediation is sound; note that unifying also changes 'BoE'->'Bind on Equip' and 'Warbound (UE)'->'Warbound Until Equipped' in the Insights CSV, which the release note should list too.

findings.title: Launcher tooltip hard-codes the brand and offers a left-click the disabled state refuses
findings.evidence: :113 hard-codes 'Ka0s Loot History' instead of NS.BRAND. :117 says 'Left-click: open the history window' even while disabled, when the click prints the refusal; and the click is a toggle, not an open.
findings.remediation: C-012: tt:AddLine(NS.BRAND, 1, 0.82, 0). Change the text to 'Left-click: show/hide the history window'. When NS.AddonIsOff(), replace it with a gray disabled line derived from NS.Slash.DisabledLine() minus the tag, not hand-built. Update tests/test_launcher.lua if it pins the tooltip text. Smoke S-008.2-3.
findings.verify_reason: core/LauncherSetup.lua:113 hard-codes "Ka0s Loot History", while :77 in the same file already uses NS.BRAND for the label. :117 says "open the history window", but onClick (:104-108) prints NS.Slash.DisabledLine() when the addon is off and otherwise calls Browser:Toggle. tests/test_launcher.lua:140/296 pin the label, not the tooltip text, so updating the test is conditional as the remediation says.

findings.title: Degraded CliResetAll clears all three id lists then only says 'unavailable'
findings.evidence: It runs NS.Filters:ClearAll() and then unavailable(), so the player is not told that the blacklist, whitelist and currency blacklist were emptied. Reachable only on a library-less install via a host caller.
findings.remediation: C-013: print 'filters reset (N ids cleared); other settings need the LibKa0s library.' using the counted return of Filters:ClearAll(). Smoke S-008.4.
findings.verify_reason: settings/Slash.lua:317-320 degraded CliResetAll calls NS.Filters:ClearAll() and then only unavailable(). modules/Filters.lua:123-131 ClearAll returns the removed count, or 0 early, so the counted message in the remediation can be built. It is reachable only in the library-less path.

findings.title: Warbound repair cannot warm the item cache for a link-only row
findings.evidence: NS.Item.LoadItem(r.itemID) with a nil itemID is a no-op, so the row stays pending until the 10-pass cap. Affects only legacy or hand-edited rows.
findings.remediation: C-014: NS.Item.LoadItem(r.itemID or NS.Item.ItemIDFromLink(r.itemLink)). Add a +1 test where the spy on C_Item.RequestLoadItemDataByID sees the parsed id.
findings.verify_reason: core/Database.lua:214 calls NS.Item.LoadItem(r.itemID). libs/LibKa0s/Item.lua:122 returns early when id is nil, so a link-only row never warms the cache, even though :210 resolves ItemBindState from the link. NS.Item.ItemIDFromLink exists (core/ItemSetup.lua:41, lib Item.lua:50). The fix is at the local call site, so routing it locally is correct. The libs citation is evidence only.

findings.title: Loot hot path allocates a gate-config table on every CHAT_MSG_LOOT
findings.evidence: A fresh { qualityThreshold = ..., ... } table is built per loot line. This matters in mass-loot bursts. Unverified: there is no perf runner.
findings.remediation: C-006 step 3: keep a module-level gateCfg table refreshed in RefreshUpvalues, and set gateCfg.itemID per call.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Collector.lua:116-119 builds a new cfg table on every loot line that reaches the gate. ShouldRecord (:41-46) only reads cfg and does not keep it, so a reused module-level table refreshed in RefreshUpvalues (:78) with itemID set per call is safe. events-frames-taint §7 (hot-path upvalue cache) is the relevant section. The perf impact is not measured, so low is the right severity.

findings.title: Database:Export claims a plain copy but shares nested tables with live history
findings.evidence: auctionPrice and sourceDetail are copied by reference. No shipped path mutates an export result today.
findings.remediation: C-015: auctionPrice = r.auctionPrice and NS.Util.DeepCopy(r.auctionPrice), and the same for sourceDetail. This is export-only, so the cost is paid once per export.
findings.verify_reason: core/Database.lua:439 (auctionPrice) and :442 (sourceDetail) are copied by reference, although the comment at :430 promises a 'plain, metatable-free copy'. NS.Util.DeepCopy exists at core/Util.lua:18. No current path mutates the export result, so it is low.

findings.title: Login prune fires HistoryChanged even when it removed nothing
findings.evidence: fireHistoryChanged() is unconditional. With the window open, that triggers about nine full-history passes 5 s after login for no change.
findings.remediation: C-006 step 4: fire only when removed > 0. Add a test that a zero-removal PruneOld sends no HistoryChanged, using a recorded-message spy that is first shown to record a positive send (red under an unconditional fire).
findings.verify_reason: core/Database.lua:797 calls fireHistoryChanged() without a condition, even when removed == 0. It is reached from the login timer (core/LootHistory.lua:82) whenever retentionDays is nonzero; the early return at :788 covers only 0. Consumers coalesce the message (Util.lua:230ff), so the cost is one set of rebuild passes, not repeated ones. Still wasted work, so low. The existing test at tests/test_database.lua:309 removes rows, so it stays green after the fix.

findings.title: Six chat lines pre-format their arguments before the shared printer
findings.evidence: The lines use ('...%d...'):format(n, ...) and 'test mode ' .. (on and 'on' or 'off') before NS.Print. All format addon-owned values, so none can meet a secret. SHOULD NOT.
findings.remediation: When these lines are next touched, pass the values as print(...) arguments instead of formatting first (optional).
findings.verify_reason: settings/Slash.lua:40/51/62/76 use ("...%d..."):format(n,...) and settings/Schema.lua:785 concatenates 'test mode ' before print. All the values are addon-owned. events-frames-taint §8 (line 143) states SHOULD NOT outside the secret-value APIs, so an info-level, optional finding is accurate.

findings.source_id: measured non-finding (01 Measurement run; 05 Known follow-ups)
findings.title: Review agent's cross-addon baseline table (2026-09-07) is out of date

findings.title: AUDIT.md step 4 fixed-High grade for the re-vendor ledger conflicts with step 5's impact grading
findings.evidence: Step 4 fixes a vendored tag with no bundle or row at High. Step 5's impact table would grade any doc-only gap Low. The audit followed step 4 for LH-62 and recorded the tension.
findings.remediation: Raise upstream in WowAddonStandards: reconcile AUDIT.md step 4's fixed High with step 5's impact-not-rule-strength grading. Either make step 4 an explicit named exception to step 5, or regrade the ledger finding by impact.
findings.verify_reason: WowAddonStandards/AUDIT.md step 4 (lines ~338-342) says 'A tag vendored with no bundle naming it and no ## Documented deviations row saying why is a **High** finding', with no mention of step 5. Step 5 (lines 857-870) says 'Grade by impact, not rule strength' and that 'A doc-only or config-only failure is Low or Info even when the rule it fails is a MUST'. A missing re-vendor bundle is a doc-only gap no user can reach, so the two steps really do conflict. The fix belongs in the playbook upstream, and info severity fits a note about the playbook's own consistency.
